scope: All Solidity sources below contracts/ except contracts/mocks/; npm dependencies are excluded.
policy: CI rejects every Critical signal and fails on every new, changed, or stale High signal. Entries document reviewed static-analysis signals; they are not blanket suppressions or claims that a source pattern is ideal.

findings.subject: BootstrapVault.finalise() arbitrary-send-erc20
findings.rationale: BootstrapVault V1 is deprecated. Its immutable ifrSource is constructor-configured, not caller-controlled; BootstrapVaultV3 is the finalized mainnet path.

findings.subject: BuybackController._addLiquidity(uint256) arbitrary-send-eth
findings.rationale: ETH is intentionally sent through the governance-configured Uniswap router and LP tokens go to the governance-configured lpReceiver. Neither destination is selected by execute() callers.

findings.subject: BuybackController._buybackAndBurn(uint256) arbitrary-send-eth
findings.rationale: ETH is intentionally sent through the governance-configured Uniswap router and purchased IFR is delivered to the immutable burnReserve. Neither destination is selected by execute() callers.

findings.subject: BuybackController.execute() reentrancy-eth
findings.rationale: execute() is nonReentrant (ReentrancyGuard, T-190) and the cooldown timestamp and execution counter are updated before external calls; a nested execute() from the router reverts (tested). The configured router remains an external trust boundary.

findings.subject: BuybackVaultV2._swap(uint256,uint256,uint256) reentrancy-balance
findings.rationale: The private _swap is called only by nonReentrant executeBuyback; all state-changing external entry points, including configuration, oracle, ownership and ETH receipt paths, share the same ReentrancyGuard. The trusted router and IFR token are immutable, constructor-validated identities; independently reviewed non-proxy implementations remain a deployment trust boundary. The before/after balance delta measures only this vault's own net IFR received during the fee-on-transfer swap, excludes pre-existing IFR and enforces minReceived before distribution. Budget, cooldown and execution count are updated before the router call, and callbacks cannot change the configuration read after it. BuybackV2 tests cover privileged router/token callbacks, pre-existing IFR, fee-on-transfer receipts/distribution and atomic rollback on short output.

findings.subject: LendingVault.liquidate(uint256) arbitrary-send-eth
findings.rationale: The liquidator bonus is intentionally paid with a checked call to msg.sender, the permissionless liquidate() caller. The function is nonReentrant, state changes precede the call, a failed payment reverts atomically, and the recipient cannot be chosen independently of the caller.

findings.subject: LendingVaultV2.claimETH(address,bool) reentrancy-balance
findings.rationale: claimETH consumes only msg.sender's ETH credit before calling the immutable, constructor-configured canonical WETH; it and every loan/asset accounting entry point are nonReentrant. The balance snapshots deliberately verify exact wrapping, exact recipient credit and restoration of the vault's prior WETH balance; failed or short wrapping reverts atomically. LendingVaultV2 H01/H03 test wrapped payout and short-mint rollback; H02 tests that a recipient callback cannot reenter claims. Canonical WETH identity remains a deployment trust boundary.
